examiner.q: You are at 400 ft on the initial climb out of LSGN, flaps 1, and the engine quits. Airfield elevation plus 1000 ft is 2500 ft. What exactly do you do?
examiner.a: Speed according to flaps setting: 78 KIAS flaps up, 73 KIAS flaps 1 notch. Maximum +- 45 degrees of RWY axis (or flight path). Full flaps when landing is ensured. Speed Vref 62 KIAS.

examiner.q: Same failure, but you are already above airfield altitude + 1000 ft (eg. for LSGN 2500 ft). What changes in the briefing?
examiner.a: Speed 78 KIAS, back to opposite runway, full flaps when landing is ensured, speed Vref 62 KIAS. Only above the airfield altitude + 1000 ft gate may a return to the opposite runway be considered.

examiner.q: Rough running on the take-off roll, before rotation. Give me the three actions from your take-off briefing.
examiner.a: Throttle idle, brakes applied, inform ATC (radio).

examiner.q: Why is a turn-back to the field forbidden low after take-off?
examiner.a: AFM: land straight ahead, making only small heading changes to avoid obstacles; never attempt to turn back to the runway, because the altitude after take-off generally does not allow it. Turn back only above airfield altitude + 1000 ft.

examiner.q: What is the maximum demonstrated crosswind for HB-KFO?
examiner.a: 22 kt (40 km/h). It appears in the checklist speed table as Xwind 22 and in the AFM as the demonstrated crosswind, section take-off in crosswind.

examiner.q: Run up: at what RPM do you check the magnetos and what are the two limits?
examiner.a: Throttle SET 2000 RPM. Magnetos — CHECKED (max drop 175-max diff 50): max 175 RPM drop between (L) or (R) and BOTH, max 50 RPM difference between (L) and (R).

examiner.q: What drop do you expect on the carburettor heat check, and at what power?
examiner.a: Carburator heater — CHECKED (drop 100), done at 2000 RPM: pull hot, check the drop of about 100 RPM, then push cold again.

examiner.q: What idle RPM must you see during the run up, and what is the last item of that check?
examiner.a: Throttle idle — CHECKED (600-650 rpm). Last item: Throttle — SET 1000 RPM.

examiner.q: The engine does not fire. What are the starter limitations?
examiner.a: Starter — DEPRESSED (max 30 sec. then wait 1'). AFM: avoid using the starter more than 30 seconds, and wait at least one minute before attempting a new start.

examiner.q: Engine has just started. What do you check, and by when must you see it?
examiner.a: Oil pressure — CHECKED RISING (green arc). AFM: if oil pressure is nil after 15 to 20 seconds, shut down and look for the cause. Green arc 3.8-6.5 bar (55-95 psi), red line idle minimum 1.70 bar (25 psi).

examiner.q: Walk me through the RPM values of the RUN UP CHECK.
examiner.a: Parking brake SET, throttle SET 1000 RPM, engine instruments GREEN ARC, area clear, throttle SET 2000 RPM for magnetos, carb heat and mixture, throttle idle CHECKED (600-650 rpm), throttle SET 1000 RPM.

examiner.q: Lined up. What power do you set and what is the minimum you must see before going?
examiner.a: Power — SET FULL (min 2200 RPM); engine instruments and annunciator lights checked. AFM normal take-off: minimum full-throttle RPM 2200, take-off speed 54 kt (100 km/h).

examiner.q: You are levelled off, leaned in cruise, and you now want to climb. What must you do first with the mixture, and why?
examiner.a: AFM: ALWAYS ENRICH THE MIXTURE BEFORE A POWER INCREASE. Care must be taken not to lean excessively, to avoid engine overheating; mixture stays full rich for take-off and climb.

examiner.q: Give me Vfe and Vfo and what each one gates.
examiner.a: Flaps (Vfe) 92 KIAS, Flaps full ops (Vfo) 81 KIAS. Flaps 1 on downwind: 'SPEED BELOW 92, FLAPS 1'. Full flaps: extend below 81 KIAS.

examiner.q: When exactly do you select flaps 2 in the standard circuit?
examiner.a: At the Point Of Descent: 'APPROACHING GLIDE' speed 85 KIAS, SPEED BELOW 81, START DESCENT, FLAPS 2, speed 80 KIAS and maintain 80 KIAS. FINAL CHECK then confirms Flaps — FULL DOWN (extend below 81 KIAS).

examiner.q: Short final, the runway is not clear. Give me the go-around sequence and speeds.
examiner.a: 'GO AROUND' — Set T/O PWR — 'SPEED ABOVE 60, FLAPS 1' — climb with 70 KIAS. AFM reference: carburettor heat cold checked, full throttle, speed 65 kt, flaps progressively back to take-off position, climb 75 kt.

examiner.q: Callouts for a touch and go?
examiner.a: Set T/O PWR — 'SPEED ABOVE 54, ROTATE' — 'SPEED ABOVE 60, POSITIVE ROC, FLAPS 1' — climb with 70 KIAS, then according to proc.

examiner.q: Why must carburettor heat never be left half way?
examiner.a: AFM: always use carburettor heat all-or-nothing (full hot or full cold); an intermediate position can in certain cases make the icing worse. Checked at run up with a drop of about 100 RPM, then pushed cold.

examiner.q: Which checklist items drive the transponder mode, and to what?
examiner.a: CLIMB CHECK item 3: Transponder — CHECK MODE 'ALT'. AFTER LANDING CHECK item 3: Transponder — CHECK MODE 'GND'.

examiner.q: Explain the 'First Push' principle and where PAT and APT apply.
examiner.a: At every change of flight phase you always start by pushing, either the elevator or the power. Entering a climb = PAT (Power, Attitude, Trim); level off from a climb = APT; entering a descent = APT; leaving a descent = PAT.

examiner.q: You are climbing at 1000 FPM to 4500 ft. When do you start the level off and in what order?
examiner.a: Anticipate by 1/10 of the ROC: with 1000 FPM start 100 ft before, i.e. at 4400 ft. Order APT: Attitude SET, Power SET, Trim SET. Power is reduced only once the speed stops increasing; trim after that.

examiner.q: On final you are below the glide path. What do you use for the angle and what for the speed?
examiner.a: Pitch controls the rate of descent / approach angle, power controls the speed, corrected simultaneously and preventively (PITCH / POWER PROPHYLAXIS). Only exception: the initial approach descent, flown 'Speed on Stick' with power at a fixed value.

examiner.q: Rolling into a turn, what do you do about adverse yaw?
examiner.a: Compensate adverse yaw with a measured rudder input in the direction of the turn, the ball showing how much — 'put rudder on the side the ball goes'. With basic training aircraft adverse yaw must always be compensated.

examiner.q: How much does stall speed increase in a 30 degree bank?
examiner.a: About +7% (eg. Vstall 60 KIAS becomes 65 KIAS). AFM table at 1000 kg, power reduced: flaps up 54 kt at 0 deg / 58 kt at 30 deg; flaps 1st notch 51 / 54 kt; flaps 2nd notch 47 / 51 kt.

examiner.q: From rotation to circuit altitude, give me the speeds and callouts.
examiner.a: Vrotate 54 KIAS 'ROTATE', climb with Vx 70 KIAS. At or above 300 ft/AAL: 'CLEAR OF OBSTACLES', 'SPEED ABOVE 70, FLAPS UP', climb with Vy 80 KIAS. Above 2000 ft/AGL: climb with Vcc 85 KIAS.

phases.title: Preflight
phases.subtitle: Walk-around done, cockpit and papers checked

items.note: AFM: baggage compartment max 40 kg, within mass and balance limits.

phases.title: Before engine start
phases.subtitle: Cockpit secured, electrics and fuel set

items.note: AFM: press both pedals, hold pressure and pull the parking brake control; release pedals, the knob must stay up.
AFM: no play or excessive friction. Steering is checked during taxi. Elevator trim: full travel, then back to take-off position.
items.spoken: Controls — stick fully forward and fully back, fully left and fully right, ailerons and elevator moving with the stick and in the correct sense, rudder free both sides, no play and no excessive friction; nosewheel steering to be checked during taxi. Controls free and correct.

items.note: AFM: total usable 109 l; 1 l unusable. AVGAS 100 LL.
items.spoken: Fuel — gauges checked, [example: one hundred and nine] litres on board out of one hundred and ten total, one hundred and nine usable, one litre unusable; at thirty-three litres per hour at two thousand five hundred RPM that is three hours eighteen minutes gross endurance, minus reserve. Quantity and endurance checked.
Fuel valve — operation checked, lever fully open, on the fuller tank; auxiliary tank lever pushed in, closed, unless required.
ELT — switch on ARM, red LED out, no red LED. ELT armed.

items.note: AFM: normal fuel pressure 35 to 550 mbar (0.5 to 8 psi).
items.spoken: Fuel pump ON — fuel pressure checked in the green, between zero point five and eight PSI, that is thirty-five to five hundred and fifty millibars.

items.note: AFM differs: selector on L for the start, then L+R (Both) once the engine runs. Fly the checklist, know the AFM.
AFM normal start: 2 or 3 injections, then throttle 1/4 forward.

items.spoken: Starter engaged — thirty seconds maximum continuous, then wait at least one minute before another attempt. Oil pressure must come up; if it is still zero after fifteen to twenty seconds, shut down and find the cause.

items.r: SET 1000 RPM (1200 RPM with engine cold)
items.spoken: Throttle set — one thousand RPM with a warm engine, one thousand two hundred RPM with a cold engine, engine steady, warming up.
Oil pressure — rising, in the green arc, three point eight to six point five bar, that is fifty-five to ninety-five PSI. If it is still zero after fifteen to twenty seconds, shut down.

blocks.title: AFM start variants
blocks.text: Hot engine: same procedure, no injections. Cold weather: sustain RPM with successive injections up to 900–1000 RPM. Flooded: fuel pump OFF, mixture CUT OFF, throttle FULL, starter a few seconds; when it fires, mixture back to RICH, then normal procedure without injection. Oil pressure zero after 15–20 s: shut down and investigate.

items.spoken: Navigation lights ON, strobe ON — all lights stay on for the whole flight, including the landing light, for conspicuity in haze, against the sun, at dusk and in busy circuits.
Alternator ON — voltmeter checked, needle in the green range, battery charging, no discharge.

Pressure indicators checked — oil pressure three point eight to six point five bar in the green, fuel pressure zero point five to eight PSI in the green, oil temperature rising towards the green, sixty to one hundred and eighteen degrees Celsius.
Annunciator lights tested — test button pressed, all warning lights illuminate, released, all lights out, no warning remaining.
Flaps — lever fully up, flaps up, indicator confirms zero, position checked visually.

Altimeters — QNH [example: one zero two one] set on both altimeters, field elevation [example: one thousand seven hundred and thirty feet] indicated on both, both agree, one hectopascal equals about twenty-seven feet.
Transponder — code [example slot: the assigned or local VFR code] set and crosschecked in the window, mode GND on the ground, ALT armed for departure, altitude readout checked against the altimeter.

items.say: Ventilation, Heater, Defroster — AS REQUIRED / Avionics — ON, SET / Directional gyro — SET

blocks.title: Gate before moving
blocks.text: Before starting to taxi, the CHECK AFTER ENGINE START must be fully completed. Flight instruments are checked in principle with the aircraft stopped; they are set during this check.

items.when: Controlled aerodrome — first call to GROUND
items.say: LOCARNO GROUND — HB-CFR — CESSNA 172 — GRASS PARKING BRAVO — VFR TO GRENCHEN — INFORMATION TANGO — REQUEST TAXI
items.note: Adapt callsign/station to local procedures.

items.say: TAXI TO HOLDING BAY — RUNWAY 26 RIGHT — QNH 1016 — HB-CFR
items.note: Read back taxi instruction, runway and QNH, ending with your callsign.

items.when: Uncontrolled aerodrome — state intention, no REQUEST
items.say: LOMMIS AERODROME — HB-CFR — CESSNA 172 — GRASS PARKING — VFR LOCAL FLIGHT — TAXI TO HOLDING POINT RUNWAY 24
items.note: Adapt callsign/station to local procedures.

blocks.title: FOR EVERY STARTING TAXI
blocks.intro: Memory items, before every taxi start.

steps.do: Taxi light — ON
Throttle — SET 1000 RPM
Parking brakes — RELEASED
Throttle — ADJUST TO TAXI WITHOUT BRAKES
steps.note: Small power increase to get moving, then reduce to hold a steady speed.

items.say: Taxi Area – CLEAR / Taxi Light – ON / Power – ….SET / Parking Brake – RELEASED
items.note: Check and announce each item; the whole area in front, beside and behind must be clear.

items.when: BRAKE CHECK — as soon as rolling for the first time
items.note: Taxi very slowly until brakes are checked. Apply just enough to feel efficiency and symmetry — the aircraft must not stop rolling.
Done only once clear of the parking area.
SPHAIR: AI – ERECTED / STABLE; DG or HDG indicator – DECREASING in a left turn, INCREASING in a right turn. Scan one instrument at a time.
items.spoken: Flight instruments checked in the turns, one instrument at a time — turn coordinator indicating the turn with the ball out, attitude indicator erected and stable, HSI decreasing in a left turn and increasing in a right turn, compass agreeing with the HSI.

blocks.title: FOR EVERY STOPPING TAXI (not on rwy!)
blocks.intro: Actions from the checklist; STOP announcements from SPHAIR ch.5.

steps.do: Parking brakes — SET
Throttle — SET 1000 RPM
Taxi light — OFF
steps.note: At every stop, leave the nosewheel in the neutral position.

blocks.title: Taxi technique
blocks.text: Nosewheel on the yellow centerline; look at the taxi line over the sighting line (eye offset ≈ 25 cm). Walking pace max on aprons, near aircraft and in turns. Headwind: elevator neutral. Tailwind: elevator pushed, power reduced. Crosswind: roll into the wind. Do not taxi with constant braking — adapt power setting accordingly.

phases.title: Run-up
phases.subtitle: Engine run-up at the holding point

items.spoken: Parking brake set — throttle set, one thousand RPM.

Engine instruments — all in the green arc: tachometer green arc two thousand to two thousand seven hundred RPM with the red line at two thousand seven hundred, oil temperature sixty to one hundred and eighteen degrees Celsius, oil pressure three point eight to six point five bar, fuel pressure zero point five to eight PSI, cylinder head temperature below the red line at two hundred and sixty degrees Celsius.
Rear and propeller area clear — throttle set, two thousand RPM, stabilised, engine instruments in the green.

Magnetos checked at two thousand RPM — right magneto, drop [example: one hundred] RPM, both; left magneto, drop [example: one hundred and twenty] RPM, both; maximum drop one hundred and seventy-five RPM, maximum difference between left and right fifty RPM, engine running smoothly. Magnetos checked, back on BOTH.

Carburetor heat — hot, pulled, drop of about one hundred RPM, no rise and no rough running, cold, pushed, RPM back to two thousand. Carburetor heat checked. Always full hot or full cold, never an intermediate position.
Mixture checked — leaned progressively until the EGT rises and the RPM starts to drop, then back to full rich, fully up, RPM restored to two thousand.
Voltmeter checked — in the green range at two thousand RPM, alternator on line, no discharge, no warning light.
Annunciator lights checked — all out, no alternator, no oil pressure, no low voltage warning at two thousand RPM.

Throttle to idle — six hundred to six hundred and fifty RPM, engine steady, no tendency to stop, oil pressure above the idle red line of one point seven bar, twenty-five PSI. Idle checked, throttle back to one thousand RPM.

phases.title: Before take-off
phases.subtitle: Last checks, then the departure briefing

items.spoken: Fuel — [example: ninety] litres indicated, usable capacity one hundred and nine litres; at thirty-three litres per hour that is [example: two hours forty-five] of endurance against a planned flight time of [example: one hour], minimum fuel on board and reserve satisfied.
Fuel pump ON — fuel pressure checked in the green, zero point five to eight PSI, thirty-five to five hundred and fifty millibars, pressure stable.
Mixture — full rich, lever fully up, and it stays full rich for take-off and climb; leaning only above five thousand feet in the climb. Always enrich before any power increase.
Elevator trim — full travel checked nose up and nose down, then set back to the take-off position, trim set for take-off.

Flaps — speed check not required on the ground, full down, second notch, travel checked, then back up to the first notch, take-off position, indicator and lever confirm first notch. Flap limit speed ninety-two knots, full flaps below eighty-one knots.

items.note: Printed CORECT on the club checklist - answer it as printed.
The briefing is the last item of this check and is normally spoken aloud.
items.spoken: Departure briefing — runway [example: two four], concrete, dry, wind [example: ten knots headwind]. Speeds: rotate fifty-four knots, Vx seventy knots, Vy eighty knots, best glide seventy-eight knots, Vref sixty-two knots; initial climb to [example: four thousand five hundred feet] direction [example: Cudrefin]. Any malfunction before rotation: throttle idle, brakes, inform ATC. Engine failure after rotation below airfield elevation plus one thousand feet: speed according to flaps, seventy-eight knots flaps up, seventy-three knots first notch, land straight ahead within plus or minus forty-five degrees of the runway axis, full flaps when the landing is assured, Vref sixty-two knots. Engine failure above airfield elevation plus one thousand feet: seventy-eight knots, back to the opposite runway, full flaps when the landing is assured, Vref sixty-two knots. Briefing completed.

blocks.title: Departure briefing
blocks.intro: Two groups: normal, then abnormal. The club publishes this briefing in French; the wording below is the SOP's own English version. Say it aloud before every take-off.

steps.do: Conditions
steps.say: Runway in use xx (concrete, grass), conditions dry (wet), wind strength and direction (eg. 10 Kts headwind)
steps.note: Fill in the actual runway, surface, condition and wind of the day before you speak.

steps.do: Speeds
steps.say: Rotation 54 KIAS, Vx 70 KIAS, Vy 80 KIAS, initial climb at xxxx ft direction x (eg. Climb at 4500ft direction Cudrefin)
steps.note: Saying the speeds aloud puts them in short-term memory - it matters most when you fly several types.

steps.do: Any malfunctions before rotation
steps.say: Throttle idle, brakes applied, inform ATC (Radio)

steps.do: Engine failure after rotation below airfield altitude + 1000 ft (eg. for LSGN 2500 ft)
steps.say: Speed according to flaps setting (78 KIAS flaps up, 73 KIAS flaps 1 notch), maximum +/- 45 degrees of RWY axis (or flight path), full flaps when landing is ensured, speed Vref 62 KIAS

steps.do: Engine failure after rotation above airfield altitude + 1000 ft (eg. for LSGN 2500 ft)
steps.say: Speed 78 KIAS, back to opposite runway, full flaps when landing is ensured, speed Vref 62 KIAS
steps.note: A turn back to land on the opposite runway is only to be considered above terrain + 1000 ft.

context.v: Before entering and when lined up

items.when: Ready at the holding point, uncontrolled aerodrome
items.note: Adapt callsign/station to local procedures.

items.when: Runway and approach clear - announcing your intention
items.say: HB-CFR, HOLDING POINT RUNWAY 24, LINE-UP AND TAKE-OFF, OUTBOUND WÄNGI
items.note: At an uncontrolled aerodrome there is no clearance: you state your intention, taking into account what other pilots have announced.

items.when: Ready at the holding point, controlled aerodrome with TOWER
items.say: HB-CFR, HOLDING POINT NOVEMBER, RUNWAY 19, READY FOR DEPARTURE
RUNWAY 19, CLEARED FOR TAKE-OFF, WILCO, HB-CFR
items.note: WILCO confirms you will make the position report the tower asked for.
SOP: the line up check is done before entering the runway and again when lined up.
SPHAIR: read the runway number (QFU) painted on the runway aloud; on parallel runways check L / C / R, and state clearly whether you line up on concrete or grass.
items.spoken: Runway [example: two four] identified — number read on the runway surface, runway heading and gyro compass compared, agreeing within five degrees; approach sectors free, wind checked.
Power set full — throttle fully forward in two to three seconds, minimum two thousand two hundred RPM at full throttle, engine instruments in the green, airspeed alive, rotate at fifty-four knots.

blocks.title: Take-off
blocks.intro: Static take-off: power is set and checked before the brakes are released.

steps.do: TO Power Set
Check RPM - min 2200 RPM
Brakes released
At Vrotate 54 KIAS, rotate to the take-off attitude
Climb with Vx 70 KIAS

blocks.title: Take-off run technique
blocks.text: Heels down, off the brakes. Power goes in smoothly over about 2-3 seconds, never abruptly, throttle full forward. Hold the centerline with rudder - the aircraft yaws left - and keep the wings level with aileron. Glance at the ASI (airspeed rising), then back to the runway and the distant reference point. Never pull the aircraft off the ground.

blocks.title: Rejected take-off
blocks.text: Abort immediately if the engine does not reach the minimum power during the take-off run. Engine failure before VR, or just after leaving the runway, means stopping on the runway remaining; on a short runway, take the best ground in the runway axis. Rule of thumb 50/70: 70% of take-off speed reached by mid-runway.

phases.title: Initial climb
phases.subtitle: 300 ft AAL to the climb check

items.when: Speed checked, obstacles passed, climb attitude stable
items.note: Flap retraction gives a brief loss of lift - correct with a small attitude change - then the speed builds as drag drops.
Above 2000 ft/AGL: climb with Vcc 85 KIAS.
SPHAIR: switch the electric pump off only at the climb check, earliest 500 ft/AAL, and check fuel pressure in the green - if the mechanical pump had failed, the engine would stop.
items.spoken: Fuel pump OFF — climb stabilised, and not before five hundred feet above the field; fuel pressure still checked in the green, zero point five to eight PSI, engine running smoothly.
Transponder — mode ALT selected and checked, altitude reporting on, code [example slot: the code set before departure] still displayed.
Power — full power checked, throttle hard against the forward stop, engine instruments reading normal values, climb speed eighty knots; above five thousand feet, lean the mixture for the climb.

blocks.title: Finished by 1000 ft AAL
blocks.text: Normally the procedures and checks after take-off should be completed by 1000 ft above ground: flaps up and the auxiliary fuel pump off. You decide the moment for the climb check and for switching the landing lights off. Keep scanning the engine limitations - oil temperature, cylinder head temperature - throughout the climb.

blocks.title: First turn
blocks.text: The climb check ends the take-off phase. Unless something else is prescribed, the first turn is not started below 500 ft/AAL. The criteria are the VAC, the shape of the terrain and local noise rules.

phases.title: Crosswind turn
phases.subtitle: First turn — lookout, announce, climbing turn

blocks.title: First turn to crosswind
blocks.intro: The take-off phase ends with the CLIMB CHECK; the first turn comes after it.

steps.do: Climb straight ahead on the runway axis until the first-turn height
steps.note: If nothing else is prescribed, the first turn is only started from 500 ft AGL. Criteria: VAC chart, terrain configuration, local noise procedures.

steps.do: Finish flap retraction and the CLIMB CHECK before turning
steps.note: Flaps up criteria: clean-configuration climb speed reached, all significant obstacles passed, climb attitude stabilised. Fuel pump off at the CLIMB CHECK, earliest 500 ft AAL, fuel pressure checked.

steps.do: LOOKOUT into the direction of the turn, then start the turn immediately
steps.note: Priority to the airspace in the turn direction. On a low-wing aircraft the outside of the turn is hidden by the rising wing.

steps.do: Roll into a climbing turn toward the crosswind leg with coordinated rudder
steps.note: Keep full power and the climb attitude; the nose-up attitude leaves a blind spot ahead and below.

steps.do: Hold Vy, roll out on the crosswind heading
steps.note: Start the rollout about 10° before the new heading.

items.when: After the lookout, before a left turn
After the lookout, before a right turn

blocks.title: Climbing turn
blocks.text: On an aircraft with little power reserve, climbing turns are flown with 15° to 20° of bank maximum; with more bank the climb becomes flatter. In a climbing turn the margin between Vx and V_STALL is very small and the critical angle of attack can be exceeded quickly.

blocks.title: Standard circuit geometry
blocks.text: Standard circuit: crosswind turn at 500 ft AAL or as defined by the local procedure; downwind parallel to the runway at 1000 ft AAL, 1 NM abeam. Circuit height, direction and headings of the local circuit must be taken from the local VAC.

blocks.title: Entry into the climb
blocks.intro: First Push: at every change of flight phase you start by pushing — either the elevator or the power. Climb entry is Power, Attitude, Trim.

steps.do: LOOKOUT — the airspace above and behind must be clear for the new flight path
steps.note: The nose-up attitude creates a blind spot ahead of and below the nose; small heading changes let you check it.

steps.do: Mixture — RICH (OR ACC AFM)
steps.note: AFM: mixture full rich for take-off and climb; above 5000 ft adjust the mixture. Checklist CLIMB CHECK: lean for climb > 5000ft.

steps.do: Climb Power — SET (REQUIRED) FULL POWER
steps.note: Fixed-pitch propeller: the climb is flown at full power, throttle fully forward.

steps.do: Climb Attitude — ADJUST FOR TYPE OF CLIMB
steps.note: Take the reference attitude known for Vx or Vy and hold it; priority to the attitude, the speed stabilises slowly and progressively.

steps.do: Trim — REDUCE LOAD ON CONTROLS
steps.note: Trim only once the aircraft and the speed are stabilised.

steps.do: Check symmetry and engine limits during the whole climb
steps.note: Put your foot on the side the ball goes. Check oil temperature and cylinder head temperature periodically.

blocks.title: Overrotation
blocks.text: A careless rotation to an unrealistic climb attitude — overrotation — makes the speed fall fast. It can drop below the chosen climb speed and the wing can even stall. Hold the reference attitude first, let the speed stabilise slowly, and trim only after stabilisation.

blocks.title: Vx and Vy with altitude
blocks.text: Vx increases by about 1/2 kt per 1000 ft gained, Vy decreases by about 1 kt per 1000 ft, so the two speeds converge with altitude. Basic training climb: full power at constant speed — the rate of climb decreases with altitude because the available power decreases.

blocks.title: Level off cruise
blocks.intro: Start the transition 1/10 of the rate of climb below the target altitude — with a ROC of 1000 fpm, begin 100 ft below.

steps.do: Anticipate the level off and announce it
Attitude — measured and continuous change toward nose down
steps.note: The acceleration phase starts; the increasing control pressure is held by hand with a progressive push on the elevator.

steps.do: Power — reduce to cruise power per the AFM performance tables
steps.note: Reduce only when the speed stops increasing.

steps.do: Trim — set, after the power reduction
Mixture — set for altitude
Landing light — AS REQUIRED
CRUISE CHECK

blocks.title: Classic errors
blocks.text: Reduce power only when the speed stops increasing. Trim only after the power reduction — trimming before makes the attitude very hard to stabilise. Reaching the target altitude at low speed and taking a level attitude straight away makes the aircraft sink: lift is not yet sufficient.

items.spoken: Altimeter — QNH [example: one zero two one] set on both altimeters, both agreeing, cruise altitude [example: four thousand five hundred feet] checked; one hectopascal equals about twenty-seven feet.

Fuel — [example: seventy] litres remaining, burn thirty-three litres per hour at two thousand five hundred RPM, [example: two hours] of endurance left, more than the time needed to destination plus reserve; check repeated at least every thirty minutes.

items.note: SOP GVMN: set cruise power 2400 RPM (max 2500 RPM).
items.spoken: Power set — two thousand five hundred RPM, sixty-five percent, thirty-three litres per hour, or two thousand four hundred RPM as the club cruise setting, two thousand five hundred maximum; tachometer inside the green arc, red line two thousand seven hundred.
Mixture set — leaned to EGT peak minus fifty degrees Fahrenheit, at any altitude; not over-leaned, engine running smoothly, and always enrich before any power increase.

items.note: Repeat the cruise check after every altitude change or significant temperature change, and at minimum every 30 minutes.

blocks.title: Mixture rule
blocks.text: ALWAYS ENRICH THE MIXTURE BEFORE ANY POWER INCREASE. Full rich for take-off and climb. Leaning in cruise after stabilisation: lower the mixture lever progressively until a slight RPM drop, then push it up slightly to restore the RPM and smooth running. Never over-lean — engine overheating.

blocks.title: Lookout before the turn
blocks.intro: Before starting a turn, run the lookout to a defined procedure. Priority to the airspace in the direction of the turn.

steps.do: Start with a head movement toward the intended turn direction
From there, scan the airspace horizontally across to the opposite direction
Raise the head and scan back the other way to check the airspace above the aircraft
steps.note: Move the head at a moderate rate — fast rotation can cause vertigo and loss of orientation.

steps.do: Announce, then start the turn immediately
steps.note: Low-wing aircraft: the outside of the turn is hidden by the rising wing.

steps.do: Roll in smoothly with aileron toward the turn
steps.note: The aileron deflection produces the roll and the aircraft starts to turn.

steps.do: Add coordinated rudder in the direction of the turn to cancel adverse yaw
steps.note: On basic training aircraft adverse yaw must always be compensated; the ball shows how much rudder pressure is needed.

steps.do: At the desired bank, stop the roll and neutralise the ailerons
steps.note: Hold a slight opposite aileron input to keep the bank steady.

steps.do: Add measured back pressure for the additional lift — do not trim in the turn
steps.note: Without back pressure the vertical component no longer balances the weight and the aircraft descends.

steps.do: Keep the ball centred: press the rudder on the side the ball goes
steps.note: Ball outside the turn: skidding. Ball inside the turn: slipping.

steps.do: Keep the lookout going, especially in the direction of the turn
steps.note: Holding the attitude on instruments must not make you neglect the airspace.

steps.do: Roll out with coordinated aileron, rudder and elevator, about 10° before the new heading
steps.note: Release the back pressure then push slightly, otherwise the aircraft climbs during the rollout. Roll out on a distant reference point.

blocks.title: Bank, speed and stall margin
blocks.text: Medium turn: 25° to 30° of bank. Up to 30° the speed loss is small — about 5 kt on a basic trainer — and is normally not compensated with power in cruise. The higher load factor raises V_STALL by about 7% at 30° of bank (example: 60 KIAS becomes 65 KIAS).

blocks.title: Starting Descent
blocks.intro: Transition to descent is A-P-T (First Push): attitude first, then power, then trim.

steps.do: Clear the airspace below and behind before leaving level flight
steps.note: Small heading changes improve the view under the aircraft.

steps.do: Set the mixture for the descent
Lower the nose to the descent reference attitude
Adjust power for the type of descent flown
Trim once the attitude is stabilised
steps.note: Trimming before the descent is stabilised makes the aircraft level off again.

steps.do: Run the DESCENT CHECK

items.note: First letters printed bold: A-A-B-C-H-E-F-F.

items.spoken: Altimeter — QNH [example: one zero two one] from the ATIS, set on both altimeters and crosschecked, transition to local procedures done, circuit altitude one thousand feet above airfield level.

blocks.title: Rate of descent
blocks.text: Long descents are flown at a constant 500 FPM, which is comfortable for healthy passengers. Short-duration descents: max 1000 FPM. Take care with ear, sinus or heart problems. POD calculation: height to lose divided by ROD = minutes; GS divided by 60 = NM per minute (120 kt gives 2 NM/min).

blocks.title: Engine care in descent
blocks.text: Power as required to obtain the desired path. Carburettor heat is used all-or-nothing, full hot or full cold; an intermediate position can make icing worse. Every 1500 ft apply a burst of power (go-around) to avoid over-cooling the engine and to clean the plugs.

phases.title: Circuit rejoin
phases.subtitle: From cruise descent to circuit altitude and speed

blocks.title: Approaching the circuit
blocks.intro: Circuit standard: from the descent to level flight at circuit altitude.

steps.do: Reduce to 90 KIAS approaching the circuit
Level off at circuit altitude
Reduce power approx 2000 RPM
Stabilise at 85 KIAS

blocks.title: Level off from the descent
blocks.text: Level off is PAT: Power SET, Attitude SET, Trim SET, then Mixture SET FOR ALTITUDE. Rule of thumb: begin the transition 1/10 of the ROD above the new level (500 FPM gives 50 ft). In the last part of the descent, preselect the power known from experience for level downwind flight.

blocks.title: Before joining
blocks.text: Except for the aerodrome circuit itself, the APPROACH CHECK is completed before integration: before the entry point or at an adequate distance from the circuit. Reduce speed to the initial approach speed before joining; the downwind is then flown speed-controlled until the approach configuration is set.

blocks.title: Integration
blocks.text: Join per the VAC procedure, which is binding in Switzerland. Standard = left hand circuit, non standard = right hand. Overfly the downwind 500 to 1000 ft above circuit altitude, observe the landing direction, descend on the dead side to circuit altitude, then integrate at 90 degrees from inside the circuit. Never descend in the downwind.

items.say: LOCARNO TOWER, HB-CFR, CESSNA 172, VFR FLIGHT FROM BERN, BRISSAGO 3000 FEET, INFORMATION SIERRA, FOR LANDING
items.note: Adapt callsign/station to local procedures.

items.say: QNH 1021, REPORT DOWNWIND, RUNWAY 26 CENTER, HB-CFR
items.note: Tower gave: JOIN AND REPORT DOWNWIND, RUNWAY 26 CENTER, QNH 1021. Adapt callsign/station to local procedures.

items.say: LOMMIS AERODROME, HB-CFR, CESSNA 172, SECTOR SOUTH 3500 FEET, VIA OVERHEAD, FOR LANDING
items.note: Adapt callsign/station to local procedures.

items.say: HB-CFR, OVERHEAD 3500 FEET, WILL JOIN DOWNWIND RUNWAY 24
items.note: Adapt callsign/station to local procedures.
Adapt callsign/station to local procedures.

items.spoken: Fuel pump ON — hand placed on the switch, switch identified, fuel pressure checked in the green, zero point five to eight PSI; approach check to be completed at the latest abeam the threshold.

Carburetor heat — as required, full hot or full cold, never an intermediate position; hot if icing conditions are suspected at reduced power, and a clearing burst of power every one thousand five hundred feet in the descent.

items.note: Start as early as possible on downwind; check completed and approach configuration established at the latest abeam threshold.
items.spoken: Speed checked below ninety-two knots — flaps first notch, approach position, selected and indicated; speed eighty-five knots on downwind, trim set.

items.note: Then speed 85 KIAS, adjust power to maintain speed, trim.
Tower answers e.g. NUMBER 1, RUNWAY 26 CENTER — read it back. Adapt callsign/station to local procedures.
Adapt callsign/station to local procedures.

blocks.title: Flap discipline
blocks.text: Glance at the ASI and call SPEED CHECKED before every flap movement - never select flaps 'in anticipation'. The extra lift causes ballooning: counter it with elevator, then trim once stable. Flaps 1 below Vfe 92 KIAS, flaps full below 81 KIAS.

phases.title: Base
phases.subtitle: Point of descent - start descent, flaps 2

items.when: At the point of descent, speed 85 KIAS

items.note: Reduce power, set the descent attitude, then speed 80 KIAS and trim.
Speed held at 80 KIAS to the final turn.

items.when: Once the approach angle can be judged
items.note: Adjust attitude to maintain glide, adjust power to maintain the intermediate approach speed.

blocks.title: Approach descent technique
blocks.text: Initial approach descent is the exception: power reduced to a fixed value, speed held with attitude ('speed on stick'). From about mid base, once the approach angle can be judged: pitch controls the descent rate and path, power controls the speed. Final approach configuration: 400-700 FPM, path 3 to 5 degrees.

items.note: Tower: WIND CALM — RUNWAY 26 CENTER — CLEARED TO LAND; read back runway and clearance. Adapt callsign/station to local procedures.
Adapt callsign/station to local procedures.
Established after the final turn if not done before.
items.spoken: Speed checked below eighty-one knots — flaps full down, second notch, landing position, indicated; final approach speed sixty-two knots Vref plus wind correction, stabilised at the latest at the start of the last third of the approach.

steps.do: Set Vfinal 62 KIAS + wind correction
steps.note: AFM: final approach speed 62 kt (115 km/h) with flaps 2nd notch, elevator trim set.

steps.do: Hold the speed with power, the approach path with pitch, and trim

blocks.title: Wind additions to Vfinal
blocks.text: Vfinal is 62 KIAS plus a wind increment: headwind over 10 kt, add one third of the headwind component; gusts, add the difference between the steady headwind and the gust peaks. The increments are not cumulative - use the larger one.

blocks.title: Aiming point and stabilised approach
blocks.text: In a stabilised descent the end of the flight vector is a motionless spot - it must sit on the aiming point at the start of the landing zone. Correct in the first two thirds, pitch and power together. Last third: stabilised on centreline and glide path, trimmed - otherwise go around.

context.v: main wheels first, in the touchdown zone

items.note: Throttle to idle smoothly, not abruptly. The aircraft becomes nose heavy - hold the aiming point. Right hand stays on the throttle until the runway is vacated.

blocks.title: Round-out and hold-off
blocks.text: The flare starts after the power gate, about 5-10 ft above the ground. Raise the nose progressively to a level-flight attitude close to the ground; no nose-down change once the round-out has started. Look well beyond the end of the runway to judge the rate of descent.

blocks.title: Touchdown
blocks.text: At about 2 m keep reducing the sink by increasing angle of attack - smoothly, never over-rotate. Hold that attitude to the end: main wheels first, in the touchdown zone. Rudder keeps the axis on the centreline, ailerons keep the aircraft over it - independent, often opposed. Heels on the floor, toes off the brakes.

blocks.title: Crosswind or strong gusts
blocks.text: Crosswind or strong gusts: flaps 1st notch, approach speed 70 kt (130 km/h) plus half the gust value. Kill the drift the classic way. Demonstrated crosswind 22 kt (40 km/h).

phases.title: Go around / Touch & go
phases.subtitle: Missed approach and touch & go standard

context.v: carb heater cold, full throttle, flaps progressively to 1st notch

blocks.title: In case of missed approach
blocks.intro: Decide early - if the approach is too high, cannot be stabilised, spacing is too tight, anything is unclear or ATC orders it, go around.

steps.do: Commit to the go around
Set T/O PWR
steps.note: AFM: carburettor heater cold (pushed) checked, full throttle. Counter the yaw with rudder.

steps.do: Check speed, then flaps 1
Climb with 70 KIAS
Set T/O PWR
Rotate
Check positive rate of climb, then flaps 1
Climb with 70 KIAS, then according to proc

blocks.title: Trim and follow-up
blocks.text: Go around control loads are heavy: first set the trim wheel to a predetermined setting known from experience, fine-tune after stabilising. Flight stability has absolute priority - handle switches only once the aircraft is under control. After every go around: Climb Check.

phases.title: Runway vacated
phases.subtitle: Stop past the separation marks, then run the check

blocks.title: Where this check is done
blocks.text: Never run the After Landing Check while still rolling on the runway or while vacating it — risk of mishandling through inattention. Vacate first, pass the marks separating the runway from the taxi area, then run it on a straight section of taxiway, normally stopped.

items.spoken: Transponder — mode GND selected and checked, altitude reporting off; check carried out after vacating the runway and passing the holding marks, on a straight section, normally at a standstill.

items.note: Adapt callsign/station to local procedures.

items.when: Tower transfers you to Ground — readback
items.note: Answer to "CONTACT LOCARNO GROUND ON 121.7". If the aerodrome has no GROUND, taxi clearance is given directly by TOWER.

items.say: LOCARNO GROUND — HB-CFR — RUNWAY 26 CENTER VACATED — REQUEST TAXI TO FUEL STATION
items.note: Adapt callsign/station to local procedures.

phases.title: Taxi in
phases.subtitle: Back to the parking, from memory

context.v: avoid exceeding 1200 RPM while oil temp is in the yellow

blocks.title: FOR EVERY STARTING TAXI
blocks.intro: From memory, every time you start rolling.

steps.do: Taxi light — ON
Throttle — SET 1000 RPM
Parking brakes — RELEASED
Throttle — ADJUST TO TAXI WITHOUT BRAKES
steps.note: Do not taxi with constant braking actions! Adapt power setting accordingly!

items.say: Taxi Area – CLEAR / Taxi Light – ON / Power – ….SET / Parking Brake – RELEASED
Parking Brake – SET / Power – ….SET / Taxi Light – OFF
items.note: Nosewheel neutral at every stop: a wheel left cocked needs excessive power to start rolling again.

blocks.title: FOR EVERY STOPPING TAXI (not on rwy!)

steps.do: Parking brakes — SET
Throttle — SET 1000 RPM
Taxi light — OFF

blocks.title: Airmanship on the apron
blocks.text: Walking pace maximum on the apron, close to other aircraft and in taxiway turns. Give way to clearly larger and heavier aircraft. Scan ahead, to the sides and behind continuously, from brake release until the parking brake is set again — you alone are responsible for avoiding a collision.

items.spoken: Parking brake set — throttle set, one thousand RPM, engine stabilised for cooling before shutdown.
Avionics master and FLARM off — the G5s switch themselves off automatically after forty-five seconds. ELT — armed, no red LED, not triggered by the landing.

items.note: AFM: magneto cut-off test is done at idle, then back to L + R (Both).
items.spoken: At idle, six hundred to six hundred and fifty RPM — magnetos off then rapidly back to BOTH; the engine hesitates, confirming both magnetos are correctly grounded, then throttle back to one thousand RPM.

items.note: Newer FR V10 revision prints this item as flaps 2nd notch.
items.spoken: Flaps — down, second notch, landing position, lever confirmed; auxiliary tank lever pushed in, closed.

blocks.title: Chocks, then release the brake
blocks.text: Once the chocks are in place, push the parking brake control back in. To set the brake: press both pedals, hold the pressure, pull the parking brake control, then release the pedals — the knob must stay in the up position. To release: push the control in.

blocks.title: Long parking
blocks.text: Hydraulic parking brakes can lose pressure during a long parking — place chocks under the wheels.
